title: Longtail Retrieval Failure Injection & Truncation Playbook
body:
Purpose:
This doc captures an experimental playbook for intentionally injecting retrieval and truncation failures to stress long-context model onboarding regressions (8k / 32k / 128k). It is intended as a reproducible set of tests and prompt sets for evaluation runs, and as a source of triage artifacts when models show attention-sink or recall collapse behaviors after rollout.

Quick summary / motivation:
- Onboarding runs occasionally show non-linear degradation when retrieval or prefix context is incomplete. We need a deterministic harness that reproduces: (a) truncation cascades, (b) retrieval backfill latencies, (c) attention sink formation when many retrieved docs contain repeated tokens.
- Goal: surface failure modes early during model verification so we can mitigate with quantization profiles, KV-cache strategies, or routing policy changes.

Test matrix (high-level):
- Context sizes: 8k (8,192 tokens), 32k (32,768 tokens), 128k (131,072 tokens)
- Retrieval shapes: 0% retrieved (cold), 25% retrieved (sparse), 75% retrieved (dense), 100% retrieved (all retrieved tokens appended)
- Failure injections: truncated-last-n-requests (drop tail prefixes), delayed-retrieval (inject latency on retrieval backend), duplicate-passages (repeat same passage 5-20x), malformed-doc (split tokens mid-token to simulate encoding drift)
- Throughput modes: single-shot, steady-stream (100 rps for 10 minutes), spike-burst (1k rps for 30s)
- Measurement windows: 99th percentile token-latency, prefix-consistency (BLEU/ROUGE against oracle), hallucination-rate (false entity emergence), attention-entropy (per-layer entropy proxy), KV-cache-hit-rate

Prompt sets (representative examples):
- Legal memo retrieval chain: multi-document prompt where answers must cite passages. Designed to reveal citation loss when truncation removes cited doc.\n  Template: [system] summarizer; [user] "Given these retrieved court opinions (listed below), answer Q and include exact citation tokens."
- Customer-support long trace: long chat history (>50 messages) plus retrieved KB snippets. Tests context stitching and conversational identity retention.
- Codebase recall: prompt expects function signatures and line references across a 120k token repo snapshot (truncated to each context size). Designed to detect pointer drift and off-by-one doc references.
- Repeated-paragraph trap: reuse a ~512-token paragraph repeated N times in retrieved set to provoke attention sink.

Failure injection methodology (how to run injects reproducibly):
1) Harness: use the onboarding stress harness (scripts/test_onboarding_stress.py) with --inject-mode flags. Harness checks out a clean model build and runs against a local retrieval emulator.
2) Retrieval emulator hooks:
   - latency-ms: add fixed or jittered delay to GET retrieval calls.
   - occlusion-rate: drop top-k retrieved docs with a deterministically seeded RNG.
   - duplication-factor: duplicate chosen passages; parameterizable per-run.
3) Truncation simulator: wraps the tokenizer and forcibly truncates the composite prompt according to specified strategies: tail-drop, middle-drop, sliding-window. Each strategy is numbered and logged.
4) Observability: attach tracing tags (onboarding.run_id, inject.seed, strategy-id) and export token-level generation traces to S3 for offline analysis.

Success and failure criteria (for automated gating):
- PASS if: prefix-consistency >= 0.85 (or domain-specific threshold), hallucination-rate increase <= 2x baseline, and 99p token latency < SLO*1.5 for steady-state runs.
- WARN if: prefix-consistency drop between 0.6–0.85, hallucination 2–5x baseline, or attention-entropy shows concentrated collapse in top-3 attention heads.
- FAIL if: prefix-consistency < 0.6 OR hallucination-rate > 5x baseline OR model emits policy-violating content during retrieval-mix tests.

Preliminary runs & observed behaviors (notes from 2024-08 test batch):
- 8k runs: generally stable. Truncation tail-drop led to predictable citation loss but graceful degradation of answer quality. Duplication-factor <= 5 had small latency increases; attention entropy remained relatively flat.
- 32k runs: spike-burst workload with duplication-factor=15 produced transient attention sink in middle layers: model repeated near-duplicate sentences and lost anchor tokens from the original user prompt (observed via token-trace). This correlated with KV-cache hit-rate dropping by ~30% when duplicate passages displaced unique fragments in the prefix cache.
- 128k runs: delayed-retrieval (200–400ms added) plus tail-drop triggered multi-turn drift where the model started privileging earlier retrieved docs (recency bias reversal). On one run the system produced a confident-but-wrong citation for a legal memo where the cited doc was actually truncated out.

Examples / snippets (token trace observations):
- Trace excerpt (32k duplication case):
  "... <USER_PROMPT_ANCHOR> ... <DUP_PARAPH X15> ... MODEL_OUTPUT: 'As noted above, the contract clause in section 4.2...'"
  Reason: anchor tokens lost because duplicate passages consumed KV-cache budget for active attention slots.

Triage checklist when failures surface:
- Re-run the failing scenario with seed=seed_id and full tracing enabled.
- Compare token-level attention maps across layers to see where entropy collapses.
- Evaluate alternate truncation strategies: prefer middle-drop or document-aware drop (drop retrieved docs that are least relevant) instead of naive tail-drop.
- Test a quantized variant to see if kernel scheduling/efficiency changes affect attention behavior (sometimes quantization reorders internal perf which can interact with runtime selection).
- If duplication triggers sink: apply deduplication at retriever level or canonicalize repeated passages before assembly.

Quick mitigations to try (ordered):
1) Retrieval de-duplication + relevance thresholding before concatenating to prompt.
2) Document-aware truncation: compute per-doc marginal utility score and drop lowest.
3) KV-cache eviction policy tweak: protect anchor tokens for current user prompt (pin anchor tokens in early KV slots).
4) Smart routing: for large-context runs with dense retrieval, route to variant with larger cache/slightly higher-latency but different kernel selection.

Open questions / unknowns to investigate:
- Is the attention-sink purely an empirical KV-cache budget effect, or an emergent transformer attention collapse triggered by repeated substructures? Need controlled microbenchmarks where only KV cache limits change.
- How do different model families behave? We need runs across at least two families: family-A (baseline verified) and family-B (new candidate) to see differential sensitivity.
- What role does tokenization mismatch play when a retrieved doc contains rare subword splits? Include malformed-doc injects and observe drift.

Action items (owners and rough ETA):
- Ethan: add deduplication and document-utility truncation hooks to retrieval emulator (ETA 1 week).
- Priya: expand prompt suite with additional legal/coding examples for 128k regression (ETA 2 weeks).
- Leo: instrument per-layer attention entropy export and integrate with Console dashboard as a temporary panel (ETA 2 weeks).
- Maya: run comparative family-A vs family-B sweep with baseline seeds and collect traces; report by next onboarding checkpoint (ETA 3 weeks).

Notes to reviewers:
- This is a working playbook — expect rough edges. The harness references a private test harness repo PR (linked above). Please add review comments in the GitHub PR for changes to inject semantics. If you run noisy experiments, please annotate run metadata with billing tags.

Appendix: reproducible command examples:
- Single deterministic run (32k, duplication=10, tail-drop):
  python3 scripts/test_onboarding_stress.py --model=family-B --context-size=32768 --inject-dup=10 --truncation=strategy:tail-drop --seed=20240829 --emit-trace=s3://redwood-onboarding/traces/20240829_run1

- Spike-burst synthetic load (128k, delayed retrieval):
  python3 scripts/test_onboarding_stress.py --model=family-A --context-size=131072 --inject-latency-ms=250 --load-profile=spike-burst --emit-trace=s3://redwood-onboarding/traces/20240829_spike1

End of doc.
